title: Chapter 12 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of performance optimization, bundle size, and Angular best practices.

questions.question: What is the default change detection strategy in Angular?
questions.explanation: The default strategy is CheckAlways (also called Default), which checks every component on every change.

questions.question: What triggers change detection in an OnPush component?
options: A new reference to an @Input property
A mutation of an existing @Input object
questions.explanation: OnPush checks when an @Input reference changes, an event from the component occurs, or an async pipe emits.

questions.question: Mutating an object passed as @Input to an OnPush child will trigger change detection in the child.
questions.explanation: The reference must change; in‑place mutation does not trigger OnPush checks.

questions.question: What is the recommended way to inform Angular that an OnPush component's state has changed outside of Angular's knowledge?
questions.explanation: `markForCheck()` tells Angular to check the component and its ancestors on the next change detection cycle.

questions.question: To reuse DOM elements when an array is replaced in *ngFor, add a ________ function.
questions.explanation: The `trackBy` function returns a unique identifier for each item, enabling efficient DOM reuse.

questions.question: Which of the following is a pure pipe's advantage for performance?
options: It runs on every change detection cycle.
It caches the output and only re‑computes when the input reference changes.
It reduces the number of service instances.
questions.explanation: Pure pipes are memoized; they only re‑run when the input changes.

questions.question: Why should you avoid calling a component method directly in a template binding?
options: It runs on every change detection cycle, which can hurt performance.
Methods cannot be called from templates.
questions.explanation: The method is re‑invoked each time change detection runs, potentially causing jank.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of AOT compilation?
options: It enables JIT compilation in production.
It pre‑compiles templates at build time, resulting in smaller bundle size and faster rendering.
It removes all CSS from the app.
It converts TypeScript to JavaScript at runtime.
questions.explanation: Ahead‑of‑Time compilation eliminates the need for the Angular compiler in the browser.

questions.question: Which Angular feature splits the app into multiple JavaScript files loaded on demand?
questions.explanation: Lazy loading loads feature modules and their code only when the user navigates to them.

questions.question: What does `PreloadAllModules` do?
options: It loads all lazy‑loaded modules in the background after the app starts.
questions.explanation: Preloading strategies load lazy chunks in the background, so navigation is instant later.

questions.question: How can you set a size limit for the initial JavaScript bundle?
options: Angular bundles are always the same size.
questions.explanation: Budgets in angular.json warn or error if bundles exceed specified thresholds.

questions.question: What is differential loading?
options: Loading different modules based on user role.
Generating separate bundles for modern and legacy browsers.
Using different change detection strategies per component.
questions.explanation: Differential loading produces ES2015+ bundles for modern browsers and ES5 bundles for older ones.

questions.question: What is the recommended file naming convention for an Angular component?
questions.explanation: Use kebab‑case with `.component.ts` suffix.

questions.question: Angular automatically sanitizes values in template bindings to prevent XSS attacks.
questions.explanation: Angular treats all values as untrusted and sanitizes them before inserting into the DOM.

questions.question: Which binding can potentially introduce an XSS vulnerability if used with user input?
questions.explanation: `[innerHTML]` bypasses Angular's template sanitization and should be used with extreme caution.

questions.question: The Angular accessibility service to announce dynamic content for screen readers is called ________.
questions.explanation: `LiveAnnouncer` from `@angular/cdk/a11y` announces messages to assistive technology.

questions.question: Which Angular CLI flag builds the app for production with optimizations?
questions.explanation: Use `ng build --configuration production` for an optimized production build.

questions.question: You should always use `OnPush` change detection for every component.
questions.explanation: OnPush is recommended for most components, but some components that depend on mutable data from parent may need the default strategy.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the `ChangeDetectorRef.markForCheck()` method?
options: It instantly re‑renders the whole app.
It marks the component and its ancestors to be checked on the next change detection cycle.
It disables change detection for the component.
questions.explanation: `markForCheck()` schedules a check for the component, even when using OnPush.

questions.question: Which tool can help you visualize the size of your Angular bundles?
questions.explanation: Tools like `webpack‑bundle‑analyzer` show a treemap of your bundle contents.
